id_and_class.summary: Epiphenomenalism holds that brain processes produce conscious experience, but experience itself causes nothing, physical or mental. Causation runs one way, from physical to phenomenal, which keeps the physical world causally closed while treating our sense that thoughts move us as mistaken.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Causally Inert Foam on the Wave

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a real by-product of biological brain activity that has no causal power of its own.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: One-way causation: physical states cause phenomenal states, never the reverse. In Chalmers’s formal statement, phenomenal properties are ontologically distinct from physical ones and have no effect on them, which makes the view a weak dualism that sits under Materialism because it affirms full causal closure of the physical.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Produced by brain activity but irreducible to it, and without downward causation
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Awareness is real, but the sense that our thoughts and intentions cause our actions is an illusion.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualia exist and are caused by the brain but cannot be reduced to physical states; they are causally idle.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: A causally closed physical world, biological brains, and phenomenal properties that are effects but never causes.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Introspection reveals experience but misleads about its causal role. Epiphenomenalism faces the problem of how we can know or report states that cause nothing, including our own beliefs about them.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Every conscious event, including conscious perception, rests on unconscious processing that does all the causal work.

mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The causal closure of the physical: every physical event has a sufficient physical cause, so conscious states can be effects of brain activity but not causes.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Conscious states accompany brain processes continuously, like foam on an ocean wave, always present and apparently active but never driving the wave.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: None. Consciousness has no causal or functional role, and there is no top-down causation from mind to brain.
core_claims_and_evidence: Physical states cause phenomenal states, but phenomenal states cause nothing.
In Libet’s experiment, the readiness potential for a voluntary movement precedes awareness of the intention to move by several hundred milliseconds, suggesting the brain initiates the act.
The Libet readiness-potential data are reproducible across many experiment designs.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical (causal closure argument), with supporting neuroscience on the timing of voluntary action.

empirics_and_critiques.known_empirical_interventions_or_tests: Libet’s readiness-potential paradigm and later replications; Schurger and colleagues’ analysis of spontaneous neural fluctuations.
empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The interpretation of Libet’s data has been challenged, especially by Schurger and colleagues, who argue that the readiness potential may reflect stochastic noise in neural activity rather than an unconscious decision. Daniel Stoljar grants that the view is counterintuitive, since our conscious states certainly seem to matter causally.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: A theory of consciousness must include a theory of mental causation, and that in turn must explain self-knowledge. If experience causes nothing, it is unclear how it shapes what we say and believe about it.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: The view sits between dualism and materialism: it admits phenomenal properties distinct from physical ones yet keeps the physical causally closed. Calling consciousness ‘entirely physical’ while also irreducible is a standing tension in the position.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since consciousness here is solely a product of biological brains, it ends when the brain stops producing it.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Conscious will does not cause action, which leaves no room for consciousness as a cosmic or causal agent.
